record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.original_question: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a useful analogue of (R4), namely an "(R4) by alteration" statement, and more generally is there a satisfactory form of "model theory by alteration" in which one is allowed to pass to finite extensions in order to recover the desired existential-closedness or decidability conclusions?

evidence.quote:
In the paper [16] de Jong proved resolution by alteration, which means that a
finite extension of the function field of the algebraic variety under consideration is
taken into the bargain.

Open problem 15: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable
(and useful) hypothesis "(R4) by alteration"? Is there a "model theory by alter
ation"?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_v$, value group $vK$, and residue field $Kv$. Recall:

(a) A place $P$ of an algebraic function field $F\mid K$ is said to admit local uniformization if for every finite set of elements $f_1,\dots,f_n\in\mathcal{O}_P$ there is a model of $F\mid K$ on which the center of $P$ is a regular point and on which all $f_i$ are regular.

(b) Local uniformization by alteration is the weaker statement that the above can be achieved after passing to a suitable finite extension $F'\mid F$ of the function field (an "alteration" in the sense of de Jong), i.e. one is allowed to replace $F$ by $F'$ before requiring smoothness of the chosen model at the (extended) center of $P$.

(c) Call a valued field $(K,v)$ an "(R4)-field" if it satisfies the model-theoretic hypothesis used to deduce existential closedness / Ax–Kochen–Ershov-type transfer results from local uniformization, namely: for every valued function field $(F\mid K, v)$ and every finite tuple from $\mathcal{O}_v\cap F$, there exists, after a suitable valuation-theoretic adjustment, a smooth model of $F\mid K$ realizing the data, allowing one to embed $(F,v)$ into an $|K|^+$-saturated extension of $(K,v)$ over $K$.

Question. Formulate and establish (or refute) an analogue "(R4) by alteration" of hypothesis (R4) in which the smooth model is required to exist only after passing to a finite extension of the valued function field, and which is implied by local uniformization by alteration. More generally, develop a "model theory by alteration": a framework of model-completeness, existential closedness and decidability transfer theorems for valued fields (in particular tame, deeply ramified, or semitame valued fields) in which one is permitted to replace function fields by finite extensions in order to recover the desired conclusions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a recent (2025) survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. While local uniformization by alteration has been established (Knaf–Kuhlmann, building on de Jong), no formulation of an "(R4) by alteration" hypothesis or a corresponding "model theory by alteration" appears in the literature, and the question is listed as open.

status_evidence.snippet: Knaf and Kuhlmann proved local uniformization by alteration (in finite extensions of the function field).
status_evidence.claim: Local uniformization by alteration is established, but its model-theoretic counterpart is not.
